message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted speed limit, but drivers must still drive at a safe speed for conditions. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system). | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Stop signs and traffic signals must be obeyed. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is generally prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, crosswalks, or within 15 ft of a stop sign. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing regulations require proper equipment and signage. | ### Where to Find the Full Text - **Texas Transportation Code** – Chapter 545 covers motor vehicle traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Offers downloadable handbooks and online resources. - **Official Texas Legislature Website** – Provides the most recent statutory updates. If you need more specific details (e.g., penalties for a particular offense, recent legislative changes, or how a law applies to a specific situation), let me know!
